newsitem.title: USA: Goldman sees yen-supportive forces intensifying.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees yen-supportive forces intensifying.

text.p: A downward correction in the yen appears due, but in the coming weeks the forces that have caused the yen to turn higher are likely to intensify, Goldman Sachs said in its Weekly Analyst comment released to clients on Tuesday.

"We feel the tide has definitely turned," Goldman economists said in the report, citing Japan's sizable April current account surplus and predicting strength in next week's Japanese industrial production data.

Goldman revised down its one-month forecasts for dollar/yen to 112 from 118 and its three-month forecast to 119 from 122. It stuck by its six-month and one-year forecasts of 110 and 105, respectively for dollar/yen.
The report noted that an interesting aspect of recent yen strength was that no evidence had yet surfaced of any negative impact on world bond markets.

"This seems to suggest that either Japanese investors have not withdrawn any existing holdings from the global bond (and equity) markets, and have perhaps just increased the degree of foreign exchange hedging, and/or that other central banks have successfully persuaded domestic investors that liquidity will be sufficient to at least compensate," Goldman said.
While admitting that some fallout in dollar/mark was inevitable given dollar/yen's precipitous drop, Goldman said it had not changed its forecasts for this rate.
"We continue to regard this as purely a yen affair," Goldman said.
Goldman is calling for a dollar/mark rate of 1.68 over a one-month horizon, 1.77 over three months, 1.65 over six months and 1.50 in one-year's time.
Goldman economists did express concern about the probable size of long dollar positions versus the mark, however, warning that at some stage there could be a "panic."
"Indeed in three months time, we would expect a mini-rerun of the yen rally to occur in the mark when there is likely to be a change in perceptions of German interest rate policy," Goldman said.
